Try the Mohoebi prototype

RSL Taxathon 2026, Challenge 1. Prepared by iNSIGHTS BI & Analytics.

Three working screens: the officer’s visits list, the trader’s app and the nil returns review. Each one tells you which user stories it covers.

Practice data only. Not connected to any RSL system.

Connect: officer visits

Pick a group, open a lead, then approve, ask for evidence or dismiss.

Covers O1O2O3O4

Assist: trader app

Switch language, check what applies, add notebook entries and tick the four habits.

Covers T1T2T3T4T5

Connect: nil returns

Open a trader who files nil returns and record the officer’s step.

Covers O6

User stories

What each user needs, and how we will know the screen does it. Stories marked with a screen can be tried above; stories marked Pilot build come next.

RSL officer

General Clients staff who decide who is contacted. Works in Connect.

  1. O1Connect, Visits

    As an RSL officer, I want to see a short list of businesses that seem to trade but are not registered, grouped by how strong the evidence is, so that I spend visits where they are most likely needed.

    Done when
    • The list can be filtered to Ready to visit, Check first or Officer to decide, with a count for each group.
    • Each row shows the area, the main sources and the score.
  2. O2Connect, Visits

    As an RSL officer, I want to see in plain words why a business is listed, so that I can judge the evidence before anyone is contacted.

    Done when
    • Opening a lead shows up to six reasons, each naming the record it comes from.
    • The sales estimate is labelled as setting priority only, never tax.
  3. O3Connect, Visits

    As an RSL officer, I want to approve a visit, ask for more evidence or dismiss the lead, so that no trader is contacted without my decision.

    Done when
    • All three actions are on the lead.
    • The list shows the new status straight away.
    • Nothing reaches a field agent until a visit is approved.
  4. O4Connect, Visits

    As an RSL officer, I want to have each of my decisions written to the case history, so that anyone reviewing the case later can see what was decided.

    Done when
    • Each action adds a line to the audit trail under the list.
    • In the pilot each line also records the officer and the time.
  5. O5Pilot build

    As an RSL officer, I want to split or correct records that were wrongly joined, for example by a shared phone, so that one trader is never confused with another.

    Done when
    • A doubtful join goes to Check first rather than Ready to visit.
    • The officer can split a group and the correction is kept.
  6. O6Connect, Nil returns

    As an RSL officer, I want to see what other records show for a registered trader who keeps filing nil returns, so that I can ask a fair question instead of assuming evasion.

    Done when
    • The list shows how many of the last 12 months were nil.
    • The suggested step is a question about closure or inactivity, or no action.

Small trader

Runs a shop, snack bar or service, often on a shared phone. Uses Assist.

  1. T1Assist, Learn

    As a small trader, I want to read which taxes may apply to my business, in Sesotho or English, without signing in, so that I understand what is asked before anyone visits.

    Done when
    • The language switch changes the screen text.
    • No sign-in is needed to read the guide.
    • Every screen says it uses practice data.
  2. T2Assist, Check

    As a small trader, I want to enter my usual monthly sales and get an indication of what may apply, so that I know which questions to ask RSL.

    Done when
    • Monthly sales are turned into a yearly figure.
    • The answer points to Simplified Business Tax, the VAT level, or asking RSL where the two overlap.
    • It says RSL decides.
  3. T3Assist, Check

    As a small trader, I want to ask an agent for help even if I am not on any list, so that I can get support on my own terms.

    Done when
    • A help button follows the indication.
    • The confirmation says an agent will contact me after an officer approves.
  4. T4Assist, Notebook

    As a small trader, I want to record daily cash, M-Pesa and EcoCash sales and the stock I buy, so that I keep simple records without a ledger.

    Done when
    • Each entry has an amount and a type.
    • The notebook shows a running total.
  5. T5Assist, Notebook

    As a small trader, I want to see which of four good habits I already meet, so that I know what earns me a tax clearance.

    Done when
    • The Trusted Trader Score shows how many of four habits are met.
    • The clearance download unlocks only at four of four and is marked as practice.

Field agent

Employed by the delivery company and approved by RSL. Uses the field visit screens.

  1. F1Pilot build

    As a field agent, I want to see only the visits an officer has approved for me, so that I never approach a trader without authority.

    Done when
    • Leads that are not approved never appear in my list.
  2. F2Pilot build

    As a field agent, I want to record the visit outcome and prepare a registration pack, so that the officer’s case is updated and registration goes through an RSL channel.

    Done when
    • Outcomes are helped, referral submitted, declined, not found or closed.
    • The outcome returns to the officer’s case.
  3. F3Pilot build

    As a field agent, I want to ask for and record consent before collecting any information, so that traders choose what they share.

    Done when
    • The visit cannot move past the consent step without an answer.
    • A refusal is recorded as declined, with no further questions.
